issues: All original 1647 claims of marriage, aversion to marriage, sexual desire, chastity or lust are historical stereotypes, not scientifically verified psychological or individual relationship facts.
This unnumbered section on whether a man marries is different from printed CXXXI, which predicts the ease or difficulty of obtaining a wife. Do not conflate or merge outcomes.
Venus and Moon are cited as source indicia of a man's marriage; this is a sex-coded seventeenth-century construction, not sex-neutral or generalizable physiology.
Barren Virgo, Gemini and Leo and fertile signs are historical astrological classes, not actual human infertility or sexual function evidence.
The author calls houses 6, 9, 12 cadent and also includes eighth expressly although it is not cadent, due to his claimed malignancy.
A majority of corroborating marriage significators is required by several negative rules; the source provides no calibrated weight, threshold or prioritization when conditions conflict.
Saturn must be very strong in the negative scenario: Lilly expressly says that if Venus and Moon outrank it in strength, the preceding no-marriage conclusion does not hold.

The author asserts a Moon/Saturn square or opposition without many other supporting testimonies is insufficient to infer singleness, even when Venus is in a barren sign. This explicit negative exception is preserved.
Original source rules conflate objective marriage history with private desire/aversion, and with reported sexual potency. They are separate outcomes requiring independent definitions and evidence.
Claims about concubines, chastity, monkhood and sexual immorality are period moral judgments, not evidence of private conduct by identifiable people.
Some original early modern sign symbols, angularity and reception relationships need specialist checking before executable numerical rule coding.
The alleged Moon combust, Saturn sign and Venus/Saturn configurations overlap with numerous exceptions; no historical denominator, negative cases or prospective test.
The seventh-house positive source includes a source assertion of sexual ability, an intimate private property never established from astrology.
No birth-time verified cohort, actual marriage registries, single-life histories, sex/gender comparison panels, self-report outcomes or blind-decoy model comparison has been evaluated.
The original first-edition body finishes at top PDF623 before numbered CHAP CXXXI; it is a substantive unnumbered seventh-house source and must NOT increment printed numbered chapter coverage.
This packet is source-anchored selective paraphrase, not a full diplomatic original glyph-by-glyph transcription or demonstration of astrological performance.
